accuracy_findings.claim: Each of your systems makes credits in three ways: taxes, the mobility bonus and buildings.
accuracy_findings.problem: Code does more than these three things. Lexes and agents also add system credits. The page's own Other sources table lists two of them, so the intro contradicts the page. The Centralization of Power lex is a sys_pop to sys_credit mul bonus (doctrine-slow.ex:92). An Erased governor with the Finance (mafioso) skill adds +5 % (character.ex:90, pushed through push_character(:governor) at stellar_system.ex:819-824). Daily mutators also hit sys_credit (mutator.ex:311, 467).
accuracy_findings.fix: Drop the count, or name the fourth source. For example: "Each of your systems makes credits from taxes, the mobility bonus, buildings and a few other sources."
accuracy_findings.evidence: grep sys_credit: doctrine-slow.ex:92 `%Core.Bonus{from: :sys_pop, to: :sys_credit, type: :mul, value: 2}`, character.ex:90 (spy :mafioso) `from: :sys_credit, value: 0.05, type: :mul`. The compiled --text output of the page shows the Other sources table with 'Centralization of Power Lex +2 Credit per Population' and 'Erased Finance Agent skill +5 % Credit'.

accuracy_findings.claim: Agent salaries and fleet upkeep are taken out of it.
accuracy_findings.problem: The credit tooltip labels these 'Agents' salaries' (resource-detail character_wages) and 'Fleet maintenance' (fleet_maintenance) in game.json:1579/1583. The behavior is right: player.ex:1199-1225 subtracts character_level_wages x level per agent and army_maintenance per Navarch with ships on board. Only the wording differs from the UI names.
accuracy_findings.fix: Use the UI names, ideally as {ui:} tokens for resource-detail labels, e.g. "Agents' salaries and fleet maintenance are taken out of it."

accuracy_findings.claim: For example, a system with 15 population pays 15 × {const:system_population_taxes_factor} = {rate:30|credits}.
accuracy_findings.problem: The result 30 is a typed literal computed from the constant. It is correct today at every speed (factor 2 at slow, medium and fast), but it will not follow the constant if the constant changes. Also, taxes use whole points, so the shot's 15.8-population fresh colony still pays 30. The example is correct as written.
accuracy_findings.fix: Optional: keep as is (verified), or note in sources that 30 = 15 x constant-slow.ex:12.
accuracy_findings.evidence: credit-acc-r0-bonus.exs, running the real Core.Bonus.apply_bonuses: 'slow: taxes=2 mob=0.1', 'medium: taxes=2', 'fast: taxes=2'. 'pop=15.8 wf=15 mob=0 -> credit=30.0 (population_taxes 30)', 'pop=15.8 wf=15 mob=10 -> credit=45.0 (population_mobility 15.0)', 'pop=30 wf=30 mob=10 -> 90.0 (taxes 60, mobility 30)', 'extra=-100 -> credit=-70, population_mobility 0' (mobility skipped on a negative subtotal).

clarity_findings.claim: The "Your income" section adds an unbriefed, unlinked mention of dominion income.
clarity_findings.problem: The guide map's brief for this section is exactly: "your empire's income is the sum of your systems minus agent salaries and fleet upkeep (one sentence)." The page instead says "Your empire's income is the credits of all your systems, plus a share of your dominions' credits. Agent salaries and fleet upkeep are taken out of it." The clause "a share of your dominions' credits" introduces dominion income (a real mechanic per player.ex:1039-1053 and the page's own sources: list) that is outside the guide map's brief for credit, has no [[link]] target anywhere in the current guide map (no dominion page exists in the Linkable pages list), and is exactly the half-explained clause rule 4 warns against ("Point instead of half-explaining... a clause that summarizes X"). It also violates rule 17 ("Every other mechanic named in the prose is a [[link]] the first time it appears") since "dominions" appears unlinked.
clarity_findings.fix: Cut the dominion clause and state the briefed sentence plainly, e.g. "Your empire's income is the sum of your systems' credits, minus agent salaries and fleet upkeep." If dominion income belongs in the manual, it needs its own page (or a section of an existing guide) added to the guide map first, then a one-sentence "See [[that page]]" pointer here.

clarity_findings.claim: The intro says credits come "in three ways" but the page has four sections that generate credits.

clarity_findings.fix: Say "several ways" instead of "three ways", or fold "Other sources" into the count ("four ways").

clarity_findings.claim: The Mobility bonus section runs one sentence longer than its guide-map allowance.

clarity_findings.fix: Merge into one sentence before the See link, e.g. "Mobility adds more credits on top of taxes, growing with the system's workforce and its mobility. See [[mobility]]."

clarity_findings.claim: The workforce aside interrupts the flow of the Taxes section.
clarity_findings.problem: "Whole points of population are the system's [[workforce]]." sits between the tax rate sentence and the screenshot/example, which reads as a tangent inside the taxes story rather than part of it.
clarity_findings.fix: Move the workforce aside to the end of the Taxes section (after the example line) or drop it, since [[workforce]] is already linked when population is first mentioned via the tax rate sentence's context.

accuracy_findings.claim: Your empire's income is the sum of your systems' credits, minus {ui:resource-detail.type.character_wages} and {ui:resource-detail.type.fleet_maintenance}.
accuracy_findings.problem: This leaves out dominions, and the code does not. Player.extract_bonus (player.ex:1037-1051) adds each dominion's credit to player_credit with from: :dominion_rate. Core.Bonus.apply_bonus (bonus.ex:21) multiplies that value by the player's dominion_rate. The base rate is 0.3 (player.ex:1012-1015, reason :initial_dominion_rate), and Lexes can raise it (doctrine-slow.ex:141 adds +0.2). So a player who holds dominions gets more than the sum of their systems. The UI even has a 'Dominions' row in the breakdown (game.json resource-detail.type.dominion). The previous draft said 'plus a share of your dominions' credits' and this round removed it, so the page is now wrong. Lexes that act on player_credit directly (for example doctrine-medium.ex:347 adds +100) are a smaller gap and fit within 'one sentence'.
accuracy_findings.fix: Put the dominion share back and keep it one sentence, for example: "Your empire's income is the sum of your systems' credits plus a share of your dominions' credits, minus {ui:resource-detail.type.character_wages} and {ui:resource-detail.type.fleet_maintenance}." You could also add 'and your Lexes' after dominions. Do not state the 0.3 rate here unless it uses a real token.
accuracy_findings.evidence: player.ex:1037-1051: `dominion_bonuses = ... Enum.flat_map(state.dominions, fn system -> ... if key in [:technology, :ideology, :credit] -> %Core.Bonus{from: :dominion_rate, value: value, type: :add, to: @key_to_pipeline[key]}` with reason {:dominion, system.name}. player.ex:1012-1015: `reason: {:misc, :initial_dominion_rate}, bonus: %Core.Bonus{from: :direct, value: 0.3, type: :add, to: :dominion_rate}`. bonus.ex:21: `is_number(input) -> input * bonus.value`, where input is the player's dominion_rate. Wages (player.ex:1200-1210) and fleet maintenance (1213-1225) are direct_last negatives on player_credit, so that part of the sentence is right.

clarity_findings.claim: The page's opening sentence, "Credits pay for buildings, ships, agent salaries and fleet upkeep," describes what credits are spent on, not where they come from — even though the guide's own brief is "Where a system's credits come from, in one story."

clarity_findings.fix: Lead with the income side, e.g. "Credit is the resource your systems produce. It pays for buildings, ships, agent salaries and fleet upkeep," keeping the rest of the intro sentence as is.
